checks: The predecessor applies to positive masses on the given consecutive actual interval for all real d≥1. The root-tail interpolation is concave there. For a nonsingleton, positivity puts the integer mean strictly between endpoints, so Jensen evaluates at the true node F_μ. Singletons give mass one and the constant is below one; two positive consecutive atoms cannot have an integer mean.

Since a_i=F_i−F_(i+1)>0, each interval of the tail-value partition has positive length. Its upper endpoint gives a strict overestimate of the integral of the strictly increasing t^p. F_(r+1)=0 is used only for the partition. Raising the strict bound 1/(p+1) to 1/p gives the asserted constant. Index reflection preserves the midpoint inequalities, gives mean −μ, and includes the μ atom in the reflected closed tail.

On any fixed positive support interval in L, w_j′=d w_j/(L−j), so μ′ is d times the covariance of j and 1/(L−j). Expanding the covariance over unordered pairs gives precisely the displayed derivative. Each summand is positive, including the pair 0,1 on all intervals with L>1. Local finiteness gives continuity at integers where a weight is born at zero, and piecewise strict increase extends across those integers. The mean tends to zero as L decreases to one.

Writing the normalized first moment on the mesh 1/L gives denominator limit ∫_0^1(1−t)^d dt=1/(d+1) and numerator limit ∫_0^1 t(1−t)^d dt=1/((d+1)(d+2)). Hence μ(L)/L tends to 1/(d+2) and μ(L) tends to infinity. For each positive integer k, continuity and strict increase give a unique L_k with mean k, and all positive indices are <L_k, so k<L_k.

At L_k the roots are affine on the actual positive integer support. Moving the lower cutoff k/L_k to 1/(d+2) changes the scaled sum by at most the cutoff difference plus 2/L_k, by counting grid points and bounding each summand by one. The integral ratio from the fixed cutoff equals (1−1/(d+2))^(d+1), and reflection realizes the same limiting value for the other tail.

For d=1 and integral L, summation gives total L(L+1)/2 and first moment L(L−1)(L+1)/6. With L=3k+1 the upper tail consists of consecutive weights 2k+1 down to 1, giving the stated rational fraction. Independently checked the two identities by integer sums for k=1 through 100.

Convexity gives inclusion of the Minkowski combination of fibers in the interpolated fiber. Brunn–Minkowski gives concavity of the volume roots along the positive support, and positivity between its extremes. Compactness makes the positive integer support finite. Dividing all fiber volumes by W scales roots by W^(−1/d) and makes the base mixed-centroid coordinate exactly the weighted integer mean. Every containing vertical cap includes the corresponding closed through-mean cap, hence the whole fiber at μ.

The cone family is a compact convex body by the norm inequality, with positive d-volume fibers κ_d(L−j)^d for j<L and zero volume at the tip if it is integral. The factor κ_d cancels in the centroid and mass fraction. The cap x≥k contains the true mixed centroid and has exactly the scalar limiting ratio. The strict inequality over W/e follows from log(1+s)<s at s=1/(d+1).
